scope: Technical sponsor fit and bounded adaptation research only; no implementation or external messaging.

inputs.edition_handling: All eight prizes are treated as user-confirmed ShellHacks 2026 offerings. Mixed year labels were not re-investigated.
inputs.assumptions: Four people, 36 hours, software-first; individual skills and account access are unknown.
inputs.eligibility: Technical fit does not establish entry eligibility, simultaneous-entry eligibility, judging criteria, credit access or award likelihood. Confirm with the separate rules research.

rating_definitions.strong natural: The sponsor technology directly implements an important part of the stated workflow or a small coherent adaptation; this is a qualitative engineering judgment.
rating_definitions.conditional useful: Useful when a named addition or deployment need is real; ordinary hosting/domain support stays conditional and is not equal to a distinctive sponsor demonstration.
rating_definitions.weak forced: Little benefit within the existing scope, unnecessary infrastructure, or a substantial unrelated change just to target a prize.

matrix.name: FormTrail
matrix.adaptation: Keep one form and deterministic completeness rules. Optionally add source-grounded simplification or spoken instructions; retain the original text and accessible controls. Cloud drafts only if cross-device use is tested.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Read approved instructions aloud with captions and playback controls; useful access option, not the completeness engine.

Gemini API.rationale: Simplify only supplied instructions with source references; never generate institutional requirements or decide eligibility.

Solana.rationale: One student's draft and checklist require no shared on-chain trust or payment rail.

Tiger Data.rationale: Sparse form drafts have no meaningful time-series or aggregate workload.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the accessible guide; a secure API is needed only if adding model calls or cloud drafts.

Snowflake API.rationale: Alternative to Gemini for source-grounded explanations; use one model provider for this role.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: One primary store for versioned drafts if cross-device persistence is in scope; local storage suffices for the base MVP.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A memorable domain can aid demo access after the guide works; check the prize's registration path.

matrix.name: Contract Canary
matrix.adaptation: Preserve the replay-and-field-diff core. Add an optional explanation grounded in an explicit trace, or a small persistent regression history. Do not turn one flow into a generic autonomous debugging agent.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Narrating a JSON diff adds little to the developer's visual replay task.

Gemini API.rationale: Explain an already-detected failure from mapped fields and replay evidence; deterministic checks remain authoritative.

Solana.rationale: API fixture comparisons do not need wallet ownership, token incentives or blockchain consensus.

Tiger Data.rationale: Useful only if repeated replay runs produce time-stamped latency/failure series with a real comparison view; twelve static mutations do not justify it.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host a runnable public fixture demo and API; keep arbitrary user code execution outside scope.

Snowflake API.rationale: Alternative model endpoint for evidence-grounded trace summaries, not a second explanation service.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: Store versioned fixtures and replay records if saved collaborative runs matter; files suffice for the original local demo.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: Domain supports a shareable developer demo; it is independent of causal debugging quality.

matrix.name: Counterexample Arcade
matrix.adaptation: Keep the exhaustive bounded enumerator and animation as the product. Optional narrated steps or grounded hints are small additions; avoid AI-generated counterexamples as the proof.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Narrate the exact current pointer state with captions; controls must work without audio.

Gemini API.rationale: Give a hint derived from the verified failing trace, with correctness checked against the enumerator.

Solana.rationale: No assets, payments or trust problem justify on-chain game state.

Tiger Data.rationale: A finite teaching exercise produces too little temporal data to justify time-series infrastructure.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Deploy the browser game; a static site is sufficient unless model hints are added.

Snowflake API.rationale: Alternative model for constrained hints; the API does not establish counterexample minimality.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: Single-session finite examples and local progress do not need a cloud document database.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A short domain makes the exercise easy to reach; registration eligibility is a separate check.

matrix.name: WindowWise
matrix.adaptation: Retain the six verified service records and deterministic interval solver. An optional natural-language request parser can turn an errand into explicit fields that the user confirms before calculation.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Read the computed plan and its conflict in plain language; retain visible times and sources.

Gemini API.rationale: Parse a user's request or draft source extraction into a schema for confirmation; never invent office hours.

Solana.rationale: Campus errand feasibility has no decentralized settlement requirement.

Tiger Data.rationale: Office-hour intervals are not a time-series analytics need at this six-record scale.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the planner and source-dated records; cloud hosting is useful support rather than the solver.

Snowflake API.rationale: Alternative to Gemini for confirmed request extraction; do not add a second AI pipeline.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: Useful as the only store if staff can update shared service records; static JSON suffices for six fixed records.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A campus-relevant domain aids access; name availability and the prize's allowed domain route remain unverified.

matrix.name: PantryRelay
matrix.adaptation: Use Atlas as the sole inventory/reservation store with atomic conditional updates or a transaction, idempotent collection, and explicit expiry processing. Show the last-item race live; omit AI and blockchain.

ElevenLabs.rationale: An optional spoken pickup confirmation can help a busy volunteer, with visible confirmation and no sensitive names read aloud.

Gemini API.rationale: The bounded inventory/hold/collection workflow gains little from generative decisions.

Solana.rationale: A single pantry is an authoritative operator; wallets and on-chain reservations add friction without solving its stated problem.

Tiger Data.rationale: Could be the sole PostgreSQL backend instead of Atlas; trend analytics are a stretch and do not justify a duplicate store.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the API, student sessions, volunteer view and expiry worker; reliability matters more than extra cloud services.

Snowflake API.rationale: Warehouse or LLM features do not solve inventory atomicity; omit them.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: Atomic inventory/reservation updates and idempotent pickup directly implement the core promise; test concurrent claims and expiry.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A short domain helps students reach the reservation demo after consistency works.

matrix.name: LostLink
matrix.adaptation: Use Gemini image/text embeddings for retrieval and a bounded image-attribute explanation; keep the found-item catalog, metadata and vectors in Atlas. Compare with a keyword/color baseline and demonstrate absent items and similar bags.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Read candidate attributes on request with matching text; do not announce a model score as proof of ownership.

Gemini API.rationale: Multimodal embeddings and image understanding directly serve photo/description retrieval and visible matching/conflicting attributes.

Solana.rationale: Matching a found object does not establish ownership; putting a claim on-chain would not fix that gap.

Tiger Data.rationale: The thirty-item visual catalog is a retrieval workload, not meaningful time-series analytics.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the catalog UI and server-side model API calls; keep credentials out of the browser.

Snowflake API.rationale: A vision-capable Cortex model can replace the Gemini attribute-extraction role; account/model access must be checked and duplicate inference is unnecessary.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: One catalog stores item attributes and embeddings and performs vector retrieval with metadata constraints; avoid a second database.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A memorable domain supports the public catalog demo; registration does not improve match quality.

matrix.name: LineCheck
matrix.adaptation: Choose one extraction path: Gemini structured document/image extraction, or Snowflake API-backed extraction. Compare confirmed fields with deterministic arithmetic and support source page/crop links only when verified; use two layouts and synthetic documents.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Dense side-by-side quantities and prices benefit more from visible source review than an added voice layer.

Gemini API.rationale: Document/image understanding plus structured fields serves extraction; human confirmation and deterministic reconciliation remain necessary.

Solana.rationale: A ledger cannot establish whether OCR text or an invoice is correct; no decentralized settlement is needed.

Tiger Data.rationale: Can be the sole relational record store if the team prefers SQL; time-series aggregates are unnecessary for ten pairs.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host uploads, source preview and server-side inference; keep the scope to synthetic supported documents.

Snowflake API.rationale: Cortex vision inference or staged document parsing gives a substantive alternative extraction backend; confirm the required API route and source-location limits.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: Could store document metadata, confirmed fields and review events as the only operational database; do not add it to a complete Snowflake store merely for a category.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A domain makes the review demo reachable but is independent of extraction and matching evidence.

matrix.name: Pulse Path
matrix.adaptation: Do not select the original hardware build under the software-only assumption. A clearly renamed audio/visual cue-learning simulator can preserve cue-response replay, but it is a changed prototype and cannot substantiate tactile learning.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Spoken or audio cue patterns fit a software audio-maze variant; this is not the original tactile device and needs captions/alternative controls.

Gemini API.rationale: Four authored cues and deterministic responses require no language model.

Solana.rationale: Cue-response practice has no on-chain trust, payment or ownership need.

Tiger Data.rationale: Only useful if repeated software sessions create a meaningful latency/error timeline; fifty bench cycles alone do not justify a backend.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the explicitly labeled simulator and replay view.

Snowflake API.rationale: LLM or warehouse setup adds little to a four-cue practice game.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: A sole session/replay store is useful for multi-session comparison; local storage is enough for one demonstration.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: Domain can support the software variant, but does not recover the original physical interaction.

matrix.name: StormTable
matrix.adaptation: Keep every scenario fictional and deterministic. A focused adaptation stores report/decision events and freshness/resource histories in Tiger Data, then replays the same events and explains stale evidence; optional scripted voice briefings can follow.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Voice scripted situation reports with captions and explicit simulation labels; do not generate unscripted safety instructions.

Gemini API.rationale: Parse player-written reports into reviewable fields or summarize a completed deterministic run; do not generate authoritative hazard outcomes.

Solana.rationale: A classroom simulation has no external trust or asset-transfer requirement.

Tiger Data.rationale: Timestamped reports, freshness queries and resource histories naturally support replay; use one SQL store and explicit refresh semantics, not unsupported speed claims on a tiny fixture.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host the fictional scenario and replay service; the rules can still run locally.

Snowflake API.rationale: A grounded post-exercise summary can use Cortex as the only LLM provider; it must cite recorded events and not override the rules.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: An alternative sole event/state store if Tiger Data is not chosen; do not maintain both just for prize breadth.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A domain can make the exercise easy to join, with simulation labeling visible.

matrix.name: BranchBridge
matrix.adaptation: Keep the authored mystery and deterministic shared state; give roles distinct ElevenLabs voices with captions. Atlas can persist the room and decision trail, with duplicate-action and reconnect checks. Avoid generated plot logic.

ElevenLabs.rationale: Distinct character dialogue is part of the cooperative story experience; generate from the authored script and cache audio with captions.

Gemini API.rationale: Constrained clue hints can use only already-revealed evidence; never let a model change the canonical branch state.

Solana.rationale: The short cooperative mystery has no economy or transferable assets; adding either changes the project.

Tiger Data.rationale: Three choices in one short scene do not need time-series analytics.

DigitalOcean.rationale: Host synchronized rooms and the session API; demonstrate two browsers and reconnection rather than decorative infrastructure.

Snowflake API.rationale: Alternative to Gemini for bounded character hints; generated story state remains out of scope.

MongoDB Atlas.rationale: One shared room record and durable decisions support atomic choice handling, idempotency and reconnect recovery.

GoDaddy Registry.rationale: A memorable domain is useful for joining a two-role demo; check registration requirements separately.

cross_cutting_findings: Do not sum ratings into a win-probability score; neither prize judging weights nor team strengths are established.
Use one primary persistence layer. Tiger Data, Atlas and Snowflake are alternatives when they would duplicate the same records.
Use one model provider per role. Gemini and Snowflake can be alternate extraction/hint paths; running both adds cost and integration risk without automatic value.
Solana is weak/forced for all ten current scopes. Do not add wallets, tokens, an economy or on-chain hashes solely to claim the category.
DigitalOcean and GoDaddy can support nearly any web demo, but deployment and naming alone do not imply a competitive Best Use entry.
StormTable is the clearest Tiger Data adaptation only if freshness/history/replay is implemented visibly; six records do not justify performance claims.
BranchBridge is the clearest ElevenLabs adaptation; PantryRelay is the clearest non-AI Atlas transaction demonstration.
Pulse Path's original hardware concept does not fit the software-only assumption. Its simulator must be clearly presented as a different prototype.
Every adaptation is proposed, not built, evaluated or guaranteed feasible for an unspecified team.

two_deep_dive_candidates.name: LostLink
two_deep_dive_candidates.recommendation: First candidate for a team with web/API and retrieval experience; strongest direct combination of Gemini visual retrieval and Atlas catalog/search. This is a fit judgment, not a probability of winning.
minimal_stack: Gemini API: image/text embeddings; optional bounded attribute extraction
MongoDB Atlas: sole catalog, metadata and vector index
DigitalOcean App Platform: browser app and server API if deploying
GoDaddy Registry domain: optional after the working demo
avoid: Tiger Data for a tiny static catalog
An ElevenLabs layer before retrieval is useful
four_person_split: Staged data, held-out evaluation and demo
two_deep_dive_candidates.hour_3_gate: One alternate photograph retrieves plausible candidates; embeddings and Atlas vector index are accessible; a keyword/color baseline exists. If access or measured value fails, keep the honest text/attribute version and reconsider the Gemini/Atlas claim.
two_deep_dive_candidates.mvp_36h: Thirty staged objects, image or text query, top-three candidates, visible agreeing/conflicting attributes, ambiguous/no-match state and no property-release workflow.
two_deep_dive_candidates.verification: Use the original twenty held-out alternate-photo queries including at least five absent items. Calibrate any retrieval threshold on separate development examples; report top-three success for present items, false matches for absent items and latency. Do not describe a similarity score as ownership probability.
two_deep_dive_candidates.demo: Distinctive bottle; two similar backpacks; then a missing object. Show the keyword baseline and whether visual retrieval actually helps. Show a candidate's attributes in the stored record.

competition.overlap: NotLost already advertises photo-based object recognition and automated matching.
competition.implication: LostLink is not a new category and cannot claim AI lost-and-found matching as globally novel.

two_deep_dive_candidates.defensible_position: An auditable campus-scale prototype whose demo makes ambiguity, conflicting visual attributes and no-match behavior explicit. This is a proposed presentation/evaluation focus, not evidence that competitors lack those features.
two_deep_dive_candidates.next_validation: Ask a campus lost-property operator whether ambiguous lookalikes and incomplete descriptions cause meaningful work; the need and operator adoption are not established.

two_deep_dive_candidates.name: LineCheck
two_deep_dive_candidates.recommendation: Second candidate if at least one teammate can preserve document source locations and build an extraction evaluation. Larger integration risk and more mature competition than a plain visual-search demo.

stack: Gemini API extracts candidate fields from two supported document layouts
Deterministic arithmetic and explicit line identifiers reconcile reviewed values
One primary store only if persistence is needed
minimal_stack_options.note: The source trail must be verified with known page/crop coordinates or actual parser locations; schema output alone is not evidence.

stack: Cortex REST vision model handles extraction, or an agreed API route invokes staged document parsing
Snowflake stores extraction/review records if already used
Deterministic reconciliation runs in code or SQL
DigitalOcean hosts the review interface if useful
minimal_stack_options.note: Confirm the prize's acceptable API route. AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT documents page content and image extraction boxes, not a guarantee of every text line's bounding box.

avoid: Combining both extraction providers solely for prize count
Atlas plus Tiger Data plus Snowflake storing identical review rows
Payments, tax decisions or fraud labels
two_deep_dive_candidates.hour_3_gate: Extract line ID, quantity and unit price from a supported pair; preserve a verified source page/crop; test account/model access. If location recovery fails, narrow to known layouts with explicit coordinates or a manual field-confirmation fallback.
two_deep_dive_candidates.mvp_36h: Two layouts, one currency, ten synthetic pairs, page/crop-linked fields, human correction, deterministic quantities/prices/totals and clear extraction-error versus true-mismatch states.
two_deep_dive_candidates.verification: Keep twenty seeded discrepancies plus clean controls; report extraction error rate separately from reconciliation precision/recall and use one held-out variation inside the supported layout family. A manual correction must remove a false extraction alert while retaining a true changed quantity.
two_deep_dive_candidates.demo: One quantity change plus one OCR ambiguity. Correct the ambiguous field, watch its alert disappear, then inspect the real discrepancy on both source pages.

competition.overlap: DocuClipper already advertises PO extraction, two-way line matching, review and mismatch flags.
competition.implication: Source-aware invoice reconciliation is a crowded workflow, not a new product category.

competition.overlap: Rossum already documents configurable invoice-to-PO line matching.
competition.implication: Do not claim that matching rules or human review are unique features.

two_deep_dive_candidates.defensible_position: A narrow transparent teaching/demo workflow that separates extraction uncertainty from exact arithmetic discrepancies. Whether that focus is differentiated for a real buyer is unvalidated; do not state competitors lack it.
two_deep_dive_candidates.next_validation: Ask a small-organization bookkeeper which supported document pair and review bottleneck actually matters; do not infer demand or financial benefit from a seeded fixture.

lighter_fallbacks.name: BranchBridge
lighter_fallbacks.when: Choose if the team is stronger in narrative/UI and real-time web state than OCR/embeddings.
lighter_fallbacks.stack: ElevenLabs authored voices + Atlas room record + DigitalOcean deployment. No LLM-generated branch logic.
lighter_fallbacks.reason: Clear audible sponsor role and a bounded two-role demo, though voice cache, captions and synchronization still need testing.

lighter_fallbacks.name: PantryRelay
lighter_fallbacks.when: Choose if the team is comfortable with database consistency and wants an AI-free product.
lighter_fallbacks.stack: Atlas as sole transactional store + DigitalOcean API.
lighter_fallbacks.reason: The last-item race, duplicate pickup and expiry are concrete correctness claims that can be demonstrated and tested.

sources.title: Gemini image understanding
sources.supports: Image understanding and structured detection/attribute workflows. Image outputs are predictions requiring evaluation.

sources.title: Gemini embeddings
sources.supports: Current docs describe gemini-embedding-2 multimodal embeddings with image and text in a shared space; verify account access before selecting it.

sources.title: Gemini document understanding
sources.supports: PDF vision and document extraction; source location accuracy must be validated separately.

sources.title: Gemini structured outputs
sources.supports: JSON schema formatting is supported, but values may be semantically incorrect and require application validation.

sources.title: MongoDB Vector Search Overview
sources.supports: Embeddings can be stored in documents and searched; use the same embedding model/dimensions for catalog and query.

sources.title: Transactions
sources.supports: Single-document operations are atomic; multi-document transactions are available and depend on appropriate read/write concerns. A database choice alone does not implement idempotency or expiry.

sources.title: Text to Dialogue
sources.supports: Text-to-dialogue provides expressive multi-speaker audio, a direct fit for authored character dialogue.

sources.title: Create dialogue API
sources.supports: The endpoint converts text/voice-ID pairs into dialogue audio; useful for an authored-script pipeline.

sources.title: Continuous Aggregates: Incremental Materialized Views for Time-Series Data
sources.supports: Official technical guide explains precomputed continuous aggregates and real-time mode. Since TimescaleDB 2.13+, materialized-only is the default; newest data needs refresh or explicit real-time aggregation.

sources.title: App Platform
sources.supports: Managed application deployment from repositories or container images; appropriate for the web/API component without adding redundant databases.

sources.title: Cortex REST API
sources.supports: API inference uses an account URL, token and available model. Supported vision models accept image inputs; availability and credentials are implementation gates.

sources.title: AI_PARSE_DOCUMENT
sources.supports: Parses staged documents into OCR text or layout, with optional page splits. Documented coordinates concern extracted images; do not infer guaranteed per-line text bounding boxes. A SQL function is not automatically the exact sponsor-required REST integration.

sources.title: Transactions
sources.supports: Solana offers signed atomic transactions/instructions. None of the ten scoped concepts has a demonstrated need for decentralized shared state.

sources.title: GoDaddy Registry homepage
sources.supports: Registry operates domain namespaces; a registered domain is a naming/deployment addition, not an application API. Prize-specific allowed registration route is unverified here.

sources.title: NotLost product homepage
sources.supports: Product advertises AI object recognition from photos and automated lost-property matching. This overlaps the central LostLink concept; marketing performance claims were not independently validated.

sources.title: Purchase Order Data Extraction
sources.supports: Product advertises PO field and line-item extraction plus invoice-to-PO matching, editable review and mismatch flags. This overlaps the central LineCheck concept; marketing accuracy claims were not adopted.

sources.title: Two-way PO Matching With Custom Function
sources.supports: Official product documentation covers captured invoice lines, purchase-order lookup and configurable exact/fuzzy/tolerance line matching.

source_caveats: Only official vendor documentation/product pages support product capability and competition claims.
The Tiger Data docs endpoint returned a web-parser content-type error; the cited official Tiger Data technical guide was accessible.
All competitor claims are vendor descriptions, not independent performance tests.
Current model/plan/region access still needs a real account smoke check; no accounts were created or services purchased.
No domain availability, registration eligibility or multi-category eligibility was established by this research.
